segments.title: Chương 126
segments.content:
Chapter 129: The Birth of a Bestselling Book

Numb.

Chen Guiliang's hand was numb!

His wrist and arm, in particular, were sore and aching.

Seeing that the queue was too long, Li Xunhuan signaled to the hired shills that they could gradually leave early. Their commission would be paid in full.

The passersby at the back, realizing the wait would be too long, also began to leave the line from time to time.

But occasionally, other passersby would join to fill the gaps.

Chen Guiliang didn't even have time for lunch, mechanically signing his name at lightning speed.

There were also a few individual fans who asked him to write a message of good wishes.

These were usually genuine fans, whose requests had to be fulfilled.

Fortunately, not many phones had camera functions in those days, and few people carried cameras around. Otherwise, being asked for a photo during the signing would have been even more trouble.

After signing five or six hundred books, Chen Guiliang had only received four requests for a photo.

"Let's go."

Hu Zhenyu glanced inside.

He had also gotten Chen Guiliang to write a blessing. He was too embarrassed to say he was the Cao Cao from that day, but on a whim, he said, "President Chen, care for an in-person game?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Sure, let's see if you can wait until I'm done signing."

So, Hu Zhenyu stood outside and waited.

Wait for what!

He'd probably have to wait for several hours.

"Let's go, let's go, we'll find a place to play in person," said the student whose username was "Chest Breaking a Big Rock."

Eighteen people had signed up on the Legends of the Three Kingdoms Baidu Tieba, but seven had bailed, so only eleven showed up today.

The female office worker, on the other hand, was queuing quite enthusiastically.

To be precise, she was chatting quite enthusiastically with the middle-aged man behind her.

Through their slightly contrived small talk, it was revealed that this man was a mid-level manager at a foreign enterprise.

They had many topics in common, discussing the highly popular, high-brow books of the time. For example: *Wolf Totem*, *We Three*, *The Da Vinci Code*, and so on.

As for figures like Nalan Xingde and Cangyang Gyatso, they wouldn't be hyped up for another couple of years.

"Your wife won't call and rush you for queuing so long?" the female office worker said.

The middle-aged man smiled, "Sometimes when she goes shopping at the mall, she forgets to even eat lunch. She's with her best friend today, and they'll definitely go for beauty treatments, so it won't matter for a while whether I'm there or not."

The female office worker was quite envious of that kind of life, "Then you still accompany your wife out shopping?"

The middle-aged man said, "I just go with her at the beginning, then I head to the lounge area to read and drink coffee. I discovered a good book today, so I came over to join the fun. I didn't expect to run into you, Miss Zhang."

The female office worker covered her mouth and chuckled, "I didn't expect it either, to just run into someone and have so many common interests to talk about. My colleagues, they don't like to read, so I usually don't have much to talk to them about."

"People should read more. It's a way to change gears after work, elevate your thinking, and broaden your horizons," the middle-aged man said.

The female office worker, as if she had met a kindred spirit, delightedly took out her phone, "That's what I think too. Can I have your number? I don't mean anything by it, I just want to find someone to share reading experiences with."

The middle-aged man also took out his phone and said, "*The Kite Runner*, which translates to *Zhui Fengzheng de Ren*. This book is exceptionally well-written, you can check it out when you have time."

"I'm sorry, I don't know that book. Where can I buy it?" the female office worker asked.

The middle-aged man seemed to have just realized, "Oh, there's no Chinese translation in the country yet. I read the English version."

"Wow, you're amazing!"

"It's alright. I bought it on a business trip to the US last year. It's extremely popular over there, sales have already surpassed *The Da Vinci Code*."

This adulterous pair had hooked up!

They were over 1200th in line. With 300 shills in front of them having already left in batches without their signatures, they were effectively over 900th in line.

In less than two hours, it was the female office worker's turn.

The female office worker observed Chen Guiliang up close and found this entrepreneur to be very handsome. Plus, he was a current student at Peking University, so he definitely had a great future ahead of him.

Unfortunately, she was a bit too old.

"President Chen, I really like your book. I've already read part of it online," the female office worker said glibly. In reality, she only knew the book had a high online readership from the promotional content on the book sash.

Chen Guiliang offered a polite smile and signed with a flourish, saying, "Thank you." While signing, he added a blessing: *Forever beautiful, may you always be smiling.*

The female office worker was overjoyed. These few words were more valuable than the book; she could take a picture and post it on her blog.

The middle-aged man didn't say much. He took the signed book and left, heading off with the female office worker to find a place for coffee.

Around noon, more than half of the queue suddenly dispersed, as people left to eat because they couldn't wait any longer.

Most of these people did not return after their meal.

But there were some who felt that they had waited for so long and had finally made it to the front, and leaving midway would be a waste of effort. So they persevered on empty stomachs, some of them not even knowing why they were queuing!

Around one in the afternoon, Chen Guiliang felt he was about to complete his task.

But as he signed on, the queue inexplicably began to grow longer again...

By three-thirty in the afternoon, the line finally disappeared, with only one or two people coming over occasionally.

Bian Guanyue took out some bread and milk, "Have something to fill your stomach. The boxed lunches are already cold."

"Damn, this is more tiring than studying for my senior year finals," Chen Guiliang complained, shaking his wrist.

Li Xunhuan smiled, "Tomorrow we fly to Shanghai, there's another one."

"My hand is probably going to be useless," Chen Guiliang said, then asked, "How many did we sell?"

Li Xunhuan said, "You signed around 3,500 copies, but that doesn't include copies that people bought at Sanlian Bookstore to get signed. To be honest, it far exceeded my expectations. There's something magical about this place."

How could it not be magical?

In the future, this place would become the top choice for celebrity signing events!

Whether selling books or albums, inexplicable passersby would always show up to queue.

"How much was the venue fee?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Xunhuan said, "30,000 yuan a day. And that's after I haggled. The mall's initial asking price was 50,000 a day."

So expensive!

Although over 3,000 copies were signed and sold today, for Li Xunhuan, it was purely a money-losing venture to generate buzz.

But it was a necessary promotional expense.

The next day, Chen Guiliang flew to Shanghai and signed books until his hand cramped.

The grand spectacles of both signing events were captured by reporters, and newspapers immediately began paid promotions.

Li Xunhuan truly dared to let the reporters exaggerate wildly. The over 3,000 copies signed in Beijing became "eight thousand copies sold on the first day" in the newspapers.

He also came up with gimmicks like "The Hottest Book of Early 2005," "A Feast of Knowledge for All," "The Author with the Highest Royalties in the Country," and "The Most Fashionable and High-End Reading Material."

Li Xunhuan also paid for sponsored articles in the book sections of portal websites like NetEase and Sina.

For a time, *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* was hyped into a massive hit.

There were also follow-up media reports, which Li Xunhuan no longer needed to pay for.

Once momentum was built, some media would always come to ride the coattails.

This was especially true for newspapers and magazines at the time, many of which had book sections that regularly recommended books. Since *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* was hot, they naturally recommended it too.

Guangming Road, Xinhua Bookstore.

A middle-aged couple walked in with their middle-school-aged son.

The boy was dejected and completely joyless, because today was for buying study materials for the winter vacation.

"Stand up straight, what do you look like all hunched over?" the mother chided.

The father said, "Don't look so glum. I'll buy you a set of extracurricular books today too."

The mother immediately added, "Buy world classics. They're perfect for improving your essay-writing skills."

The boy sighed silently.

The mother found a clerk, "Where are the study materials and world classics?"

The clerk pointed the way.

As the family walked further in, they were struck by the sight of a whole row of *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty*, with a sign marking it as the "Bestsellers Section."

The father stopped and pointed at the promotional poster for his wife, "Look."

The mother took a closer look, "Recommended by experts and professors from both the Academy of Social Sciences and Peking University, and so many other authors too. Can a kid understand this book?"

The father pulled out a copy and first looked at the title page and preface.

The mother continued to look at the poster, lecturing her son, "Look at him, coming from the countryside, so diligent and hardworking. He was specially recruited by Peking University and even passed their admission score on his own. He's only a freshman, yet he's started a company and written a book. And you? All you know is how to play games!"

The boy also casually flipped open a copy and saw the Legends of the Three Kingdoms bookmark inside.

It looked like a game, and it seemed very fun.

"Mom, let's just buy this one. I want to learn history," the boy said.

The mother read the first chapter and found that even she could understand it, "This book is not bad, suitable for middle school students. You can learn some general historical knowledge from it too."

The boy was overjoyed.

From time to time, people would stop in front of the bookshelf; the spot was simply too conspicuous.

Gradually, seven or eight students on winter break gathered there. They didn't pay for the books, just stood there reading slowly, capable of standing for a whole day without even eating lunch.

Some got tired of standing and simply sat on the floor, leaning against the bookshelf.

More and more people gathered, and as the popularity grew, even those who weren't interested couldn't help but come over for a look.

Every now and then, a customer would pick up a copy to purchase.

The book market was very prosperous in those years, and many people were willing to buy and read books. Several bestsellers had been released in succession.

Not only was the foot traffic in Xinhua Bookstores huge, but even shops in small county towns that specialized in pirated books would often become extremely crowded during holidays.

Of course, this was the final blaze of glory for the Chinese book industry.

Starting from some unknown year, the number of people visiting bookstores began to dwindle, and one after another, both legitimate and pirated bookstores closed down. Those that struggled to survive mainly relied on children's books and educational materials.

Although Chen Guiliang's version of *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* wasn't popular enough online yet, it couldn't stand up against the sheer number of customers in brick-and-mortar bookstores.

He was living in an era when the book market was thriving!

Early one morning, while Chen Guiliang was still asleep with Bian Guanyue in his arms, he received a call from Li Xunhuan. "President Lu, I just got back to Beijing two days ago. Don't tell me you want me to organize another book signing."

Li Xunhuan's voice was excited, "It's a huge hit! As soon as I launched those promotional activities, and since your book has no reading barrier, sales in all major bookstores have been climbing steadily. Some of the more popular bookstores asked me for a restock after just two or three days!"

"It's all thanks to President Lu's brilliant methods," Chen Guiliang flattered.

Li Xunhuan said, "A large number of media outlets are now following the trend with their own reports. It's all spontaneous promotion that I didn't pay for. *Sprout* magazine is also building momentum for you, calling you the new literary star they've cultivated."

"I know about that. They also invited me to an event during the summer vacation," Chen Guiliang had already agreed, as it was right to return the favor.

Li Xunhuan continued, "There are also a few TV stations that have proactively contacted me to invite you onto their shows. Of course, they won't pay an appearance fee. Think of it as free, mutually beneficial publicity."

Chen Guiliang said, "Help me pick two or three reliable ones. We'll skip the ones that are too low-brow."

Li Xunhuan laughed heartily, "Now you're ordering me around like I'm your agent."

(End of this chapter)
